record.what_it_does: Messaging platform with a Bot API and MTProto user-client API for building bots and clients.
record.auth_notes: Bot API: a per-bot token from BotFather, passed in the URL path. MTProto user API: api_id/api_hash from my.telegram.org plus phone-number login (code, then 2FA via SRP) to get a user session. There is no OAuth2 for acting on a user's account. A multi-user toolkit would use bot tokens, with users messaging the bot. Acting as a user needs the MTProto session flow, which carries ban risk.
record.access_notes: Bot tokens are free and instant via BotFather. api_id/api_hash is free at my.telegram.org, limited to one api_id per phone number. There is no review step for bots. User-account automation via unofficial clients is monitored, and flooding or spam can get an account banned.
record.api_breadth_notes: The Bot API is an HTTP API with roughly 100+ methods: messages, media, chats, inline mode, payments, stickers and more. The MTProto API (TDLib) is far broader and covers full user-client functionality. I did not count the methods exactly.
record.mcp_notes: I found no official Telegram MCP server. Community servers include chigwell/telegram-mcp, sparfenyuk/mcp-telegram, overpod/mcp-telegram and lexfrei/mcp-tg. Most use MTProto user accounts.
record.blocker_notes: Bots can only see chats where users have started or added them, so they can't read a user's existing chats. Acting as a user requires MTProto phone login, which has no OAuth and carries ban risk. Bot token auth fits a multi-user toolkit poorly, because each user would have to create or supply a bot.

evidence.quote: Each bot is given a unique authentication token when it is created
we will send an HTTPS POST request to the specified URL
Log in at my.telegram.org ... API development tools
a text message containing an authorization code is sent to the user's phone using auth.sendCode

record.needs_human: The Bot API page was truncated at about 100k of 620k characters, so I did not read the full method list or the rate limits. The Bot API test environment is not confirmed. The MTProto test servers are confirmed at core.telegram.org/api/auth. The sandbox is "yes" on that basis. The community MCP search was a single search, so there may be other servers I missed. The user-account route's ToS risk needs a human decision.
